title: National Audit Office case study reports that Justice Transcribe saved probation officers time on meeting notes
summary: The NAO reports that Justice Transcribe, an AI note tool, summarized over 1,600,000 probation meetings in England and Wales, an estimated 266,667 hours saved.
account: The Ministry of Justice (MoJ) Justice AI Unit and HM Prison and Probation Service (HMPPS) adapted Minute, a meeting transcription and summary tool from the government's Incubator for AI, into Justice Transcribe for probation supervision meetings. A pilot with 40 probation officers in Kent, Surrey, Sussex and Wales ran from May to July 2025. Officers who completed the final survey reported that the tool cut the time to write up meeting notes by 73% on average, to about 5 minutes of review and editing, and 29 of 30 said that note quality had improved. Use widened from October 2025, and by the end of March 2026 the tool reached about 11,000 sentence management staff. The National Audit Office (NAO) published a case study on 14 October 2026. It reports that over 1,600,000 meetings were summarized between 7 October 2025 and 14 September 2026, an estimated 266,667 hours saved according to HMPPS. The NAO notes that HMPPS has no data on the time actually saved. These estimates rest on modeling assumptions, and HMPPS plans further evaluation. HMPPS quality checks found inaccuracies, mostly misspelled names and agencies, in 20% of the final case records that they examined.
purpose: Justice Transcribe was built to transcribe and summarize probation supervision meetings so that officers spend less time writing notes. The time saving is that purpose.
